text:
elaine: Quick question about the console hint vs runtime precedence. The console shows route A above route B because of a higher 'hint' score, but in production we still end up hitting route B due to header-anchor weighting. Is that intended?

sam: Yeah noticed that too. Console hints were supposed to be purely a UI ordering aid, not a change in match semantics. But it's confusing when customers use hints during debugging.

josh: Right — runtime uses deterministic match score: specificity -> anchor weights -> header claims -> tiebreak. Hints are ignored by the runtime today.

maria: Can we surface that distinction in the console? A small tooltip would help: "Hint = UI ordering only; runtime uses match scoring".

elaine: I agree. But two edge questions: 1) should a hint be allowed to force a fallback (i.e., prefer route with lower computed score but flagged as hinted)? 2) telemetry-wise, how do we correlate console-ordered expectations with actual matches for regressions?

sam: For (1) I think forcing would be dangerous — would break expectations for header-anchored rules and quotas. Maybe add an explicit flag: "prefer_at_runtime: true" that teams can opt into (behind feature flag).

josh: I'd prefer avoid adding another precedence layer unless there's a solid use-case. If we must, it should be explicit and gated by RBAC + telemetry to track errors.

maria: For (2) we could emit an event when console hint != runtime match: route_console_hint_mismatch {route_hint_id, selected_route_id, request_id, reason}. That would feed console UX and Optimize.

elaine: Example where this bit us: customer had two routes, path identical but one had header anchor x-region=us-east and the other had hint=100. Console showed the hinted route first; ops assumed it would be used. Production went to header-anchored route and tripped a quota.

sam: Oof. Quota gets painful. If we add any runtime-prefer flag we need to automatically check for quotas and warn: "This route is hinted but will cause quota violation vs other routes".

josh: Implementation note: our match scoring currently computes: base_score += path_specificity*1000 + host_specificity*500 + sum(anchor_weight) + header_claim_bonus. Hints are not in the formula. If we add runtime preference, we could inject a hint_score delta with an upper bound (e.g., max +200) to avoid full override.

maria: Bound makes sense. Keeps predictability. Also propose a console rollout UX: when you set prefer_at_runtime, console shows "Runtime-prefer enabled (experimental) — roll out to 10% by default" with canary controls.

elaine: Good. On telemetry side, please add a per-request tag showing which rule was 'candidate_top_by_console' vs 'selected_by_runtime' so `explain_match` traces can show divergence.

route-bot: deploy check: lint passed for match-scoring changes, unit tests covering anchor vs hint delta added. CI: ✅

sam: Next: permissions. prefer_at_runtime should be limited to org-admins + platform-engineering until we see stable metrics.

josh: Agree. Also add an automatic rollback if mismatches produce >1% error increase in 5m window.

maria: I'll draft the console copy and telemetry schema. Elaine, can you own the design for the canary UI?

elaine: Yep, I'll mock up the tooltip and canary toggle today. Will post design link when ready.

sam: Thanks — sounds like a plan. Follow-ups: josh to prototype bounded hint delta, maria to spec telemetry events, elaine for UX, and I’ll write the RBAC + rollout policy.

elaine: cool :thumbsup:
